lab_table.hypothesis: Stack the confirmed skew with downscaling for inclusion: missed inclusion are ~33px, far below the 90px train median, so scaling inclusion sources to 0.3-0.7 (yielding ~27-63px pastes) while keeping the inclusion-heavy allocation should lift inclusion AP50 beyond 0.357. Confirmed if inclusion AP50 rises by >=0.05 and mAP50 beats the 30/10/10 control, with the gain concentrated in inclusion's low-size tertile.

Diminishing returns on inclusion: after 30 cumulative inclusion synthetics, inclusion may be saturating, so shifting budget to patches (which dropped to 0.708 when starved to 10 in R1) and scratches should raise overall mAP50 more than more inclusion. Confirmed if mAP50 beats the skew candidates and patches AP50 recovers toward >=0.74 while inclusion AP50 does not collapse.

Alternative small-paste mechanism for inclusion: instead of downscaling (C1), select smaller source defects via prefer_small weighting at default scale, producing naturally small, high-fidelity pastes that match the missed 33px inclusion without the blur/contrast loss of aggressive downscaling. At identical allocation to C1, confirmed if inclusion AP50 exceeds C1's, isolating source-size selection as the better lever.
CONTROL (added by the lab): repeat your last kept plan (allocation projected onto this round's constraints).

lesson: R2: downscaling inclusion (0.3-0.7) HURT inclusion (0.326) — refuted; prefer_small sources at default scale helped inclusion (0.418 vs 0.326 at identical allocation). Rebalancing to 25/15/10 (C2) gave the best mAP50 (0.615) and best inclusion (0.421), proving the inclusion-heavy skew was over-allocated and that starving scratches to 5 is harmful (scratches wants >=10). Final round: stack the two confirmed inclusion levers — rebalanced allocation + prefer_small for inclusion — keep scratches >=10, and do NOT downscale.
